docs.title: Ferry
docs.text:
Move Umbraco content and schema between sites, reviewed before anything changes.

Code-first schema and safe content deployment for Umbraco 17, from development to staging to live.

Get started Watch the tour NuGet 
dotnet add package Ferry.Umbraco --prerelease
dotnet add package Ferry.Backoffice --prerelease

docs.title: Reviewed transfers
docs.text: Send and Get pages, media and their dependencies between sites. Every change is planned and shown first. Items arrive as drafts, or published when you choose. Send a whole tree from the Content or Media root in one action.

docs.title: Schema as code
docs.text: SchemaBuilder migrations and generated C# migrations keep document types, data types and templates identical on every environment, with drift reported.

docs.title: Packages and snapshots
docs.text: Export offline .ferry.zip packages, import them by drag and drop or at startup, and keep restore points.

docs.title: Safe on real sites
docs.text: Fingerprinted reviews that can be used once, per-site permissions, one operation at a time and a recovery journal for every apply.

docs.title: Extensible
docs.text: Value mappers for your own property editors and package providers for data outside content. Skybrud redirects and Umbraco Forms included.

docs.title: Free to use
docs.text: Free for any site, including commercial work, under the Ferry Freeware License. Needs no other synchronisation tool.

docs.title: See it in action
docs.text: Two sites, one reviewed Send: the options, the review, the result on the target, and a repeat that changes nothing.

docs.title: Built into the backoffice
docs.text: Review every create, update and dependency before it is applied. Sites: pair with a code and grant each peer only what it needs. Queue items across the tree and send them together.

docs.title: Try it in three steps
docs.text:
1

Install on each site.

dotnet add package Ferry.Umbraco --prerelease
dotnet add package Ferry.Backoffice --prerelease

2

Register Ferry in Program.cs.

builder.CreateUmbracoBuilder()
    .AddBackOffice()
    .AddWebsite()
    .AddComposers()
    .AddFerryUmbracoFull()
    .Build();

3

Connect the sites: on one, Settings › Ferry › Sites › Create pairing code (tick Allow two-way to connect both directions); on the other, Connect a site and paste it. Codes work once. Then pick a page, Actions › Send to…, and review.

Read the overview Extend Ferry

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to Ferry. Versions follow Semantic Versioning; while Ferry is pre-1.0, minor versions may contain breaking changes.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Send with the published version no longer fails with HTTP 500 on an unpublished page. A page that was published and then unpublished keeps an old published version id in Umbraco but has no published name, and the export sent a null name. Ferry now treats such a page, and a page never published, as having no published version.
  • Sending a tree (for example Send everything) with the published version leaves out the pages that have no published version, and the review names them ("N pages were left out because they have no published version: …"). A page selected on its own without one is refused by name and key; a published page below a left-out one fails, naming both. The full-site export names the pages it leaves out the same way.
  • A page with no name to send is reported by name and key instead of failing the export.
  • A transferred relation type is found on the receiving site straight away. Its relation type and relations were stored, but Umbraco's cached set of relation types still predated the apply, so they were not found until the site restarted.
  • The note naming left-out pages is shown to administrators only: a delegated editor's selection can reach pages outside their grant.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: • Each release is checked against the packed packages by every end-to-end suite and the browser tests, and by a check that every Ferry endpoint was called successfully.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Atomic apply (Full adapter). Each apply batch (one push batch, one Pull, one package import or one restore) runs in one Umbraco scope on the receiving site, media and view files included. The DraftText adapter is unchanged: it writes item by item. A cancelling Saving/Publishing/Moving handler, failed validation or any error rolls the whole batch back; the result says nothing was kept. Saved and Published handlers run once per batch, after the commit. If one throws, the batch stays saved and is reported Completed with a warning, and Ferry refreshes the cache and search index for the batch.
  • Handler messages. The message a handler on the other site gave when it cancelled a save, publish or media save reaches the apply and publication results, operation history and the backoffice.
  • Large-apply warning. A Pull, package import or restore above Ferry:Backoffice:LargeApplyWarningItems (default 1,000 written items; Unchanged and schema items do not count) says that it applies in one transaction and that editors on the site cannot save while it runs; the review asks for confirmation. The apply is never refused on size.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Document-type inheritance is kept on the target: an inherited type is no longer placed in folders named after its parents, and Inheritance no longer becomes Composition (F1).
  • Document-type folders keep their keys across sites (F2).
  • New content and media are created with their values in the first save, so a handler that checks required values accepts them; the source sort order is kept (H1-c).

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
• Upgrade both sites. Until both run this version, inherited document types in folders show Update on every transfer.
  • Site Saved/Published handlers now see a batch at once, after the whole batch is saved, instead of one item at a time between Ferry's writes.
  • A long Pull, package import or restore blocks backoffice editors on that site while it runs: on SQL Server their saves fail after Umbraco's 5 s lock timeout.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Redesigned Sites page in Settings › Ferry. This site shows the site's name, address and role (Development, Staging, Live or Other); Ferry:Backoffice:SiteRole fixes the role in configuration (Set in configuration), and configured destinations can declare Ferry:Backoffice:Destinations:<id>:Role.
  • Connected sites table. One row per site, joining our connection and their access key: role badge, address, what we may and they may do (Send, Get, Publish, Compare), and status (online, unreachable with the reason, not checked, Check again). Edit changes name, role, Get and their permissions and has separate Revoke their access and Stop connecting; Disconnect does both. A site managed in configuration can only have their key revoked here. Saving unchanged permissions leaves the key (and approvals bound to it) untouched.
  • Connect a site validates the pasted pairing code as you paste (site, what it allows, two-way, hours left, or why it cannot be used), lets you set the new site's role, and for two-way codes choose what the other site may do and edit this site's address. No pairing code? keeps the address and key fallback, now with a role too.
  • Let another site connect. Create a pairing code with permission chips and two-way wishes; it is shown once with Copy. The codes table shows Waiting (hours left), Used by and Expired, with Revoke or Remove.
  • Compare permission. A new read-only peer permission for item inventories, implied by Send or Get on access keys and by Preview or Export on configured peers. Nothing uses it yet; the compare view comes in a later release. Policy hashes are unchanged, so existing approvals and durable jobs stay valid.
  • Site tests also report whether the other site lets this site publish.
  • Connecting (by pairing code or address and key) to a site that is already a configured destination is refused with a message, so the Sites page never shows one site twice; a pairing code is not used up by the refusal.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• The separate Access keys and Pairing codes not used yet lists are gone. Every access key now appears as a row in Connected sites: edit its permissions there and revoke it with Disconnect.
  • The pairing-code list API now also returns used and expired codes, kept for 30 days.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: • Redesigned transfer panel for Send, Get and the queue: Choose (site cards, what to send, version, language chips and option switches with help), Review (summary tiles, always-visible notes and warnings, schema changes as a change table) and Done (links to the items, Undo this get after a Get). Loading placeholders, progress for large sends, Try again after an error and an empty state when no site is connected. The queue offers the same version and language choices (when it holds pages) and the same option switches as a single transfer.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • Publish after sending counts only published pages as already up to date: "Sent 1 changed item and published 4 pages (3 already up to date) on Target." Before, the unchanged count included every dependency in the review.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Paired sites are no longer all named "Ferry". Pairing codes and claims name this site with the new optional Ferry:Backoffice:SiteName, otherwise its host (e.g. staging.example.com, localhost:49191), set by the server instead of the browser page title.
  • Review notes use the singular for one note ("1 note — it does not block sending").
  • Unresolved-reference notes name the item that links to the missing one, and shorten the missing item's key: "Unresolved reference to Media 279fdd7b… in Content “Home”: …".
  • Publish after sending says what was sent and what was published: "Sent 1 changed item (3 unchanged) and published 4 pages on Target", with singulars.
  • The Connect a site wizard shows its first step as one sentence instead of one line per fragment.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Send or get a whole tree. Administrators get Send everything to… and Get everything from… on the Content and Media section roots. Each opens the usual transfer panel with every top-level item and its descendants selected; Content brings its dependencies and referenced media, Media sends only the media library. Large sends split into batches as before.
  • Publish after sending. Content sends (single items, the queue and whole-tree sends) offer Publish on after sending to administrators when the destination supports publication. After the send, Ferry reviews and publishes the selected items and their child items (not dependencies) in the sent cultures, and reports "Sent N items and published M on ". A publication review with errors is not forced: the drafts stay and the review opens. Not available for background sends. Preview operations now carry their parent key, and GET connections/{id}/publication-support tells administrators whether a destination can publish.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Pairing codes work once and can connect both ways. A pairing code (ferry2.…) is now a one-time invitation that expires after 24 hours, not the access key itself. The site that pastes it redeems it at the new POST /ferry/v1/pairing/claim; the issuing site then creates a new access key and records which site used it. A second use says "This pairing code was already used. Create a new one." With Allow two-way, the other site's admin can grant access back in the same step, and both connections are saved. ferry1.… codes are refused (breaking).
  • The Sites tab lists unused pairing codes with their expiry, and access keys with the site that used them; both can be revoked. Create an access key instead still issues a plain key for connecting by address.
  • POST access-keys no longer returns a pairing code; pairing uses the new pairing-codes and servers/pair management endpoints. Existing access keys and connections keep working.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The add-to-queue message says "1 item is queued" instead of "1 items are queued" (English and Spanish).
  • Get shows its notes. The Get (pull) and package-import reviews now list the same notes as Send, such as a page pointing at media that is not in the transfer. Before, a Get silently left such references unresolved.
  • Clearer unresolved-reference note. It now says that an item deleted or in the source's recycle bin must be restored there and sent again, and that saving the page before it arrives removes the link.
  • Export failures say why. When the source cannot export a selection, the destination now shows the source's reason instead of a bare "400 (Bad Request)".

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text: • Every remaining pre-Ferry name is now a Ferry name, with no compatibility: routes /ferry/v1/…, headers X-Ferry-*, tables cmsFerry*, permissions Ferry.Push / Ferry.Pull, packages .ferry.zip, pairing codes ferry1.…, configuration only under Ferry, and no legacy file imports. Both sites must run the same version; existing Ferry data starts fresh.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Umbraco Forms file settings. Forms transfers refuse a view path outside the Forms email template folder (Forms/Emails/), and a Save as an XML file workflow whose Extension is not xml, txt or csv. Before, any relative .cshtml path and any extension that did not look like a server file were accepted (behaviour change).
  • Managed server access keys. Changing a managed server's address (scheme, host or port) now requires entering its access key again, so a stored key is never sent to a different host. Saving the same address keeps the stored key.
  • Redirect conflicts. The Skybrud redirects conflict error no longer includes the receiving site's own redirect key, which a peer with only Preview permission could read.

docs.title: Schema as generated C# migrations
docs.text:
• Generated migrations. With Ferry:Schema:Migrations enabled on a development site, schema edits in the backoffice keep a draft migration (_PendingSchemaChanges.cs, never compiled) up to date, and Create migration (Settings › Ferry › Advanced, or POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/ferry/schema/migrations) turns it into a timestamped SchemaBuilder migration and adds it to the generated plan file FerrySchemaPlan.g.cs. The first one adopts the site's whole schema; later ones contain only what changed. See generated migrations.
  • Per-environment history. Every environment runs the listed migrations it has not run yet, in step id order, at startup. A failing migration is rolled back, blocks the later ones, and is shown on the Advanced tab and by the new Ferry schema migrations health check; the site keeps running and the next start retries it.
  • Drift. Schema changed outside the migrations (for example directly on live) is listed on the Advanced tab and by the health check until it is resolved, across deploys: a migration that changes a drifted item does not hide it. Administrators can Accept current schema (Advanced tab, or POST …/ferry/schema/migrations/accept, all items or selected keys) to take the schema as it is there.
  • Create migration refuses while the plan lists migrations the database has not run, so a teammate's change is never undone by a diff against a database without it.
  • New SchemaBuilder steps: Remove…Async for every schema kind and for properties, groups, tabs and compositions; Rename…Async for document types, media types, templates, properties, groups and tabs; MovePropertyAsync. Removals refuse when stored values exist unless you pass allowDataLoss: true by hand.
  • .Folder(...) in Ensure… now moves an existing item into the stated folder (.Folder("") = root).
  • Files are written only in the Development environment, outside Umbraco's Production runtime mode, inside ProjectPath. Member types are not covered.
  • Sites with a hand-written 0.5 schema plan keep it running; to switch, create a first (adoption) migration and remove the old plan registration in the same commit.

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
• SchemaCodeExport is created through dependency injection only; its constructor is now internal. Resolve it, or ISyncSchemaCodeExport, from the container.
  • SchemaBuilder and UmbracoFullSyncStore have new optional constructor parameters. Source that calls them compiles unchanged, but code compiled against 0.5 that constructs them directly must be rebuilt (binary break).

docs.title: Behaviour changes
docs.text:
• EnsureDataTypeAsync with a stated key adopts an unused data type of the same name (re-keying it), as transfers do, instead of refusing; a namesake in use is still refused.
  • A template whose view's Layout names a plain view rather than a template is created without a master template (in SchemaBuilder and transfers), instead of failing with MasterTemplateNotFound.
  • Pages and media that no longer fit their type's root or child rules are copied where the source has them also when their type is unchanged on the destination; for media, the root and child rules are relaxed the same way as for content.
  • .Folder(...) in Ensure… moves an existing item into the stated folder; before, it applied only to new items.
  • UmbracoMediaTransfer.ValidateAsync has a new overload taking the unchanged schema items; the 0.5 overload is kept.

docs.title: Self-contained
docs.text:
• Self-contained. Ferry no longer depends on any other synchronisation package. Schema is written and read by Ferry's own serializer and importer on Umbraco's services, and property values by Ferry's own value mappers, built on Umbraco's reference tracking. Sites that also run another synchronisation tool keep working side by side.
  • Value mapper API: IFerryValueMapper and AddFerryValueMapper<T>() let you add support for your own property editors; see extending Ferry.
  • Language keys are derived from the ISO code, and built-in member property keys from the member type and alias, so every site agrees on them.
  • Transfer formats are now Full v7 / v8. Upgrade both sites together: 0.4 and 0.5 sites refuse to exchange transfers or packages with each other.

docs.title: License and distribution
docs.text:
• Ferry is now free to use and closed source, under the Ferry Freeware License: free for any site, including commercial work; no redistribution, modification or reverse engineering. Earlier builds were never published.
  • Packages ship obfuscated, without source, symbols or repository links.

docs.title: Package data in transfers
docs.text:
• Package providers: a package can add data it keeps outside content (redirects, forms, …) to Ferry transfers by implementing IFerryPackageProvider. Items keep their keys, show in the review with their changed fields, and are written after the pages and media they point at. Off by default: set Ferry:Full:AllowPackageItemTransfer on both sites. A site without the provider refuses those items before anything is written. See extending Ferry.
  • Ferry.Skybrud.Redirects carries Skybrud redirects. Destination URLs must be site paths or http(s) URLs.
  • Ferry.Umbraco.Forms carries Umbraco Forms definitions with their workflows, and accepts the form and theme pickers. Workflow view paths must stay inside the site's views, and address settings must be public http(s) URLs.
  • Ferry:Full:AdditionalMediaExtensions allows a site's own static media types (for example .pdn). Types a browser or the server can run are refused.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Templates whose Layout is a plain view rather than a template transfer, including over an existing view file.
  • Pages that no longer fit their type's root or child rules copy as the source has them when the type comes along.
  • Blueprints kept in a blueprint folder no longer stop a whole-site export.
  • The display-only Umbraco.ListView property of upgraded sites is accepted.
  • Legacy {localLink:umb://…} links in rich text inside blocks no longer block the import.
  • On SQLite, Ferry's lease renewal no longer commits in the middle of an entity write, where Umbraco's relation tracking would fail with "database is locked" after retrying for minutes.
  • Legacy {localLink:1234} links by integer id approve the page they resolve to, so the import no longer refuses them as unapproved references.
  • A page whose type varies by culture but that exists in no language is left out of a whole-site export with a warning, instead of stopping it.
  • Changing a data type's editor or storage, or changing or removing a property, is allowed when no stored value uses it (a fresh site's built-in types). Element types always count as used, since block values are stored in pages.
  • Block values written in another order compare equal.
  • A peer request refused with 422 is logged with its cause on the refusing site.
  • The "would lose or change data" message shows both values as text where they differ.

docs.title: Code-first schema
docs.text:
• SchemaBuilder covers the whole schema (#30):
  • data types, with their portable configuration;
  • templates (the view file ships with the site; the layout comes from its Layout);
  • languages, media types and custom relation types;
  • document types with tabs and nested groups, folders, allowed and default templates, list views, variations, history cleanup and every property setting. Definitions are written through the same serializers transfers use, so a migration produces exactly the schema a content-only transfer compares. Nothing is removed, and destructive changes are refused.
  • Adopt code-first on an existing site (#30, #33):
  • Settings › Ferry › Advanced › Download schema as code, or GET ferry/schema/code, writes the site's schema as one migration that keeps every key.
  • The download is a zip with one partial-class file per schema kind; format=cs returns a single file.

docs.title: Backoffice
docs.text:
• Spanish translation (#31). Every term the backoffice uses now has English and Spanish text, including the workspace tab labels.
  • The Danger zone heading contrast is fixed in the light and dark themes (#31).
  • Queue changes survive a reload (#32): clearing the queue and reloading at once no longer brings items back.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Get fixes (#29):
  • non-root pages kept their templates;
  • template layouts come from the Razor Layout;
  • .jfif, .jpe, .heic and .heif media are allowed;
  • orphan segment values are skipped;
  • FerryImport.IsActive lets site handlers skip work during an apply;
  • legacy block UDIs, SQL Server and SQLite dates, empty values and empty rich-text blocks no longer plan as updates.
  • Items Umbraco renamed "Name (n)" because a destination sibling holds the source name plan as unchanged (#32).
  • The packaged dashboard no longer imports a chunk that was not committed (#31).
  • SQLite: a durable apply could stall for minutes while its restore point was saved. Ferry's database work read and then wrote in one deferred transaction; when another request committed in between, SQLite refused the write (SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT), which waiting never fixes, and the provider kept retrying it. Ferry's write work now takes SQLite's write lock first, as Umbraco does.
  • The README now recommends SQL Server for production sites that receive transfers, or SQLite with Cache=Private (#32).

docs.title: Renamed and standalone
docs.text:
• Ferry name (#19). Packages are Ferry.Core, Ferry.Transport, Ferry.Umbraco and Ferry.Backoffice; configuration lives under Ferry.
  • Standalone package (#20). Ferry has its own workspace under Settings › Synchronisation and needs no other synchronisation package.

docs.title: Backoffice redesign
docs.text:
• Send and Get replace Push and Pull throughout the interface (#21).
  • Pickers instead of GUID fields, with a key fallback for items that exist only on the other site (#21).
  • Review screen leads with a summary ("4 new pages"), calls out schema changes, moves and templates, and keeps the full list and unchanged items behind toggles (#22); the Publish review follows the same layout (#27).
  • Overview, Sites, Packages and Advanced tabs (#23): connected-site diagram, whole-site Send and Get, activity in plain sentences, a Connect a site wizard with pairing codes, drag-and-drop package import, and a danger zone for recycle-bin moves and seeding.
  • Top-bar Ferry panel with Queue and Activity tabs, and an Add to queue action (#23).
  • Side-panel buttons sit in the panel footer (#24); compact site cards, a single Synchronisation heading, and theme-aware colours (#25); Umbraco form controls, first-run guidance, a Managed in config badge and visible keyboard focus (#27).
  • Settings-tab text is translatable through ferry_* keys (#26, #27).
  • Connection checks on the Sites tab are cached for five minutes (#26).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Editors see their own activity: GET ferry/operations/mine (#26).
  • Code-first schema: SchemaBuilder with stable, alias-derived keys (#18).
  • Content-only sites: Ferry:Full:ContentOnly rejects transfers that would change schema (#17).
  • Granular permissions on top of delegated grants (#16) and a server-side per-user transfer queue (#14).
  • Package import at startup (#12), a cluster operation lease (#11) and bulk-apply suspensions (#9).

docs.title: Fixes and maintenance
docs.text:
• Audited transitive package versions (#10) and editor reference coverage (#13).
  • The Settings workspace source is TypeScript.

docs.title: 0.1.0-alpha.1
docs.text: First experimental release: reviewed Full-mode Push and Pull, packages, snapshots, publication, delegated editors and the native backoffice dashboard. No package was published.

docs.title: Code-first schema with SchemaBuilder
docs.text:
Ship schema as reviewed code, run it once per environment as Umbraco migrations, and let Ferry move only content (enforce on receiving sites with Ferry:Full:ContentOnly).

SchemaBuilder covers what a content-only transfer compares: data types, templates, media types, document types (tabs, groups, folders, templates, variations, compositions), languages, and custom relation types between pages and media. Existing sites can switch in one step: Adopting an existing site.

docs.title: A migration
docs.text:
using Ferry.Umbraco.Schema;
using Umbraco.Cms.Infrastructure.Migrations;

public sealed class AddLanding(IMigrationContext context, SchemaBuilder schema) : AsyncMigrationBase(context)
{
    protected override async Task MigrateAsync()
    {
        await schema.EnsureDataTypeAsync("Tagline", "Umbraco.TextBox", dataType => dataType
            .EditorUi("Umb.PropertyEditorUi.TextBox").Config("""{ "maxChars": 80 }"""));
        await schema.EnsureTemplateAsync("landing", template => template.Name("Landing"));
        await schema.EnsureDocumentTypeAsync("landing", type => type
            .Name("Landing").Icon("icon-home").AllowedAtRoot().Folder("Pages").Composition("seo")
            .AllowTemplates("landing").DefaultTemplate("landing")
            .Tab("Content", tab => tab
                .Property("tagline", "Tagline")
                .Group("Hero", group => group.Text("heroTitle", required: true).MediaPicker("heroImage")))
            .Tab("SEO", tab => tab.Text("metaKeywords", name: "Keywords")));
        await schema.EnsureAllowedChildrenAsync("landing", "article", "landing");
    }
}

From 0.6 Ferry can generate these migrations from backoffice changes. Hand-written ones go in your own plan, run at startup like any Umbraco migration:

var plan = new MigrationPlan("MySite.Schema")
    .From(string.Empty)
    .To<AddSeoComposition>("add-seo-composition")
    .To<AddLanding>("add-landing");
await new Upgrader(plan).ExecuteAsync(migrationPlanExecutor, coreScopeProvider, keyValueService);

AddFerryUmbracoFull() registers SchemaBuilder.

docs.title: What the Ensure… methods do
docs.text:
Method Creates or converges EnsureDocumentTypeAsync, EnsureMediaTypeAsync Name, icon, description, folder, root and element flags, list view, variations, history cleanup, compositions, allowed templates, groups, tabs, properties EnsureAllowedChildrenAsync, EnsureAllowedMediaChildrenAsync Allowed child types, for types that allow each other EnsureDataTypeAsync Name, editor and editor UI, folder, storage, configuration EnsureTemplateAsync The template row for a view the site ships EnsureLanguageAsync Name, default and mandatory flags, fallback EnsureRelationTypeAsync Relation type between pages and/or media: name and direction. What it relates and its dependency flag are fixed once created
  • Creates missing items and converges existing ones. Never removes: unlisted groups, tabs and properties are kept, so a release can restate a type with only its additions; omitted settings keep their value. Name, icon, description and root/element flags are always stated (defaults: alias, icon-document or icon-picture for media types, empty, off).
  • Refuses (throws) changing an existing property's data type, a data type's editor or storage, or the variations of an existing type or property. Write each as its own explicit migration.
  • Stable keys. Without .Key(...), keys are RFC 4122 v5 UUIDs (SchemaBuilder.StableKey) from document-type:{alias}, media-type:{alias}, data-type:{name}, template:{alias}, relation-type:{alias}, {type}/group:{group alias}, {type}/property:{alias}, so every environment has the same identities and content-only transfers see the schema as unchanged. .Key(existingKey) adopts a hand-made item; on groups, tabs and properties it also re-keys an existing one (e.g. built-in media types on upgraded sites).
  • Unused namesakes are adopted. If no data type has the stated key but an unused one with the same name exists (e.g. a fresh install's Content Picker), it is re-keyed and converged. A namesake used by a property is refused.
  • Data type configuration is portable JSON, written through Ferry's transfer serializers. If omitted, the existing configuration is kept.
  • Folders. .Folder("Pages/Landing") moves an existing item there, creating folders as needed; .Folder("") moves it to the root; no .Folder(...) leaves it in place.
  • Templates read Views/{alias}.cshtml and never change it (missing view: Umbraco's default view). The master comes from the view's Layout, so create layouts first. A Layout naming a plain view, not a template (e.g. "HistoryTimelineLayout.cshtml"), gives no master and logs a warning. Ferry briefly writes a placeholder into the view so Umbraco can read the master, then restores the original bytes; only a migration step's scope discards it on failure, so call the template methods only from migrations.
  • Groups and tabs. Group(...) on a type is outside any tab; Tab(...) holds properties and groups; a group in a tab has alias tab/group. Use .Alias(...) when the stored alias isn't the one Umbraco derives from the name, and .SortOrder(...) when order isn't declaration order.
  • Properties outside any group (common on upgraded sites): call Property(...) or a shortcut on the type itself, e.g. type.Text("internalRemarks").Tab("Content", …). Ensure… never moves an existing property between groups; use MovePropertyAsync.
  • Property settings: Property(alias, dataTypeKey, property => …) takes Label, Describe, Mandatory (with message), Validation (with message), Vary, LabelOnTop, Order, Key.
  • Shortcuts use Umbraco's default data types by name: Text, TextArea, RichText, Number, Toggle, Date, ContentPicker, MediaPicker. Otherwise use Property(alias, "Data type name").

docs.title: Adopting an existing site
docs.text:
1. As an administrator, choose Settings › Ferry › Advanced › Download schema as code, or call:
GET /umbraco/management/api/v1/ferry/schema/code?namespace=MySite.Schema&className=AdoptSchema

This returns a zip of partial-class files: AdoptSchema.cs (the migration) plus AdoptSchema.DataTypes.cs, AdoptSchema.DocumentTypes.cs etc., one per schema kind. format=cs returns one file. In code, ISyncSchemaCodeExport.GenerateFilesAsync and GenerateAsync return the same. 2. Review, commit with the site's views, and run it as the first step of the plan. Later changes are new migrations. 3. It changes nothing on the source site and recreates the same schema, keys included, elsewhere.

The migration runs: languages, relation types, data types, templates (layouts first), media types, document types (compositions first); then allowed children; then block editor configuration (block data types are created early without configuration). Default-valued settings are omitted; ungrouped properties are stated on the type. Member types are not included (Ferry transfers them only with people).

Schema SchemaBuilder cannot state (e.g. a group containing groups outside a tab) is refused: Create migration returns 409 with the reason and writes nothing.

docs.title: Removing, renaming and moving
docs.text:
Each step is a no-op when already in the target state:

  • RemoveDocumentTypeAsync, RemoveMediaTypeAsync, RemoveDataTypeAsync, RemoveTemplateAsync, RemoveLanguageAsync, RemoveRelationTypeAsync, RemovePropertyAsync, RemoveGroupAsync, RemoveTabAsync, RemoveCompositionAsync.
  • RenameDocumentTypeAsync, RenameMediaTypeAsync, RenameTemplateAsync, RenamePropertyAsync, RenameGroupAsync, RenameTabAsync: no-op when only the new alias exists, refused when both do. RenameTabAsync renames the tab's groups too (old/x → new/x); a RenameGroupAsync in the same migration naming the old tab alias follows it.
  • MovePropertyAsync(type, property, groupAlias): empty groupAlias moves it out of every group and tab.

typeAlias resolves a document type first, then a media type. Groups and tabs are removed only when empty (a tab: no properties or groups).

A step that would lose stored values throws, failing the migration (rolled back and reported). The check runs on the deploying environment:

  • property and composition removals use Umbraco's property usage check on the owning type (for a composition, the composition or nested composition holding the property, which covers every type composed of it);
  • a data type used by any property is never removed;
  • a type with content is not removed;
  • a language is removed freely only when no type varies by culture;
  • element types (block values are not tracked) and a missing usage service count as "may hold values".

allowDataLoss: true overrides this; write it by hand, Ferry never generates it.

docs.title: Generated migrations
docs.text: Edit schema in your development site's backoffice. Ferry keeps a draft migration; Create migration turns it into a named C# migration you commit. Other environments run missing migrations at startup. Only compiled C# carries schema; content still moves with Send and Get. Covers data types, document, media and relation types, templates and languages. Member types are not covered.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Under Ferry:Schema:Migrations:

Setting Default Meaning Enabled false Run generated migrations at startup and track their schema. Turn on everywhere. HistoryName {SiteAssembly}.Schema History name, so one database can hold several sites. {SiteAssembly} is the entry assembly name. Namespace {SiteAssembly}.Schema Namespace of generated classes (assembly name, not RootNamespace). WriteDrafts false Allow writing .cs files. Development only. ProjectPath none Absolute path of the web project folder (with the .csproj). Required for writing. Folder Migrations/Schema Folder under ProjectPath for generated files.

Put WriteDrafts and ProjectPath in appsettings.Development.json or user secrets:

{ "Ferry": { "Schema": { "Migrations": { "Enabled": true, "WriteDrafts": true, "ProjectPath": "/src/MySite.Web" } } } }

Files are written only when WriteDrafts is true, the environment is Development, the Umbraco runtime mode is not Production, and ProjectPath contains a .csproj. Paths never leave ProjectPath. Otherwise Create migration is hidden.

If you change Folder, set MSBuild FerrySchemaFolder to match so the draft stays out of compilation:

<PropertyGroup><FerrySchemaFolder>Schema/Generated</FerrySchemaFolder></PropertyGroup>

docs.title: The draft
docs.text:
Every backoffice schema save, folder move or rename rewrites {Folder}/_PendingSchemaChanges.cs a few seconds later with the differences from the last migration (deleted when there are none). It is not compiled and not watched by dotnet watch, so it can't ship.

Create your migration before you pull. If teammates' migrations run on your database while you have a draft, Ferry keeps it as _PendingSchemaChanges.before-{time}.cs (not compiled), logs a warning, and regenerates the draft from your database afterwards. Where a teammate restated an item you edited, the draft shows your database's current state; check it.

docs.title: Create migration
docs.text:
As an administrator, enter a name such as AddLandingPage on Settings › Ferry › Advanced and choose Create migration (class name: capital first letter, letters and digits only), or:

POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/ferry/schema/migrations
{ "name": "AddLandingPage" }

GET …/ferry/schema/migrations/status returns history, draft and drift.

  • Writes {Folder}/{yyyyMMddHHmm}_{Name}.cs, adds it to the plan, deletes the draft, and marks it applied on your database.
  • The first migration adopts the whole schema (as in Adopting an existing site); later ones hold only changes since the previous one.
  • Step id: {yyyyMMddHHmm}-{kebab-name}. A new step always sorts last; Ferry bumps the minute on a same-minute clash or when the plan is ahead of your clock.
  • {Folder}/FerrySchemaPlan.g.cs lists every step. Never edit it by hand; on a merge conflict keep both lines.
  • Refused while the plan has migrations your database hasn't run (just pulled, or failed here). Restart first, or your migration would undo theirs.
  • Parallel branches both run, in step id order. If both restate the same item, the later one wins and the other change is lost. After merging, restart, check the item, and add a fix-up migration if needed.

docs.title: What happens at startup
docs.text:
Ferry keeps its own per-environment history (not Umbraco's single "last step").

  • Every unrun migration runs in step id order, each in its own scope, whatever the merge or deploy order.
  • Afterwards Ferry refreshes content type and data type caches and rebuilds the published cache once the site has started ("Ferry refreshed the content type caches…"). Each run logs "Ferry schema migrations finished in … ms".
  • A failing migration does not stop the site. Its database writes, template view files and Umbraco's in-memory caches are rolled back, so steps must derive from AsyncMigrationBase (UnscopedAsyncMigrationBase is refused). The failure is logged, shown on the Advanced tab and in the Ferry schema migrations health check, and blocks later migrations. It retries on next start; fix the migration and redeploy.
  • Load balancing: only the scheduling publisher runs migrations. Register an IServerRoleAccessor returning SchedulingPublisher on one server and Subscriber on the rest (builder.SetServerRegistrar<T>()). With Umbraco's default election roles are Unknown at boot, so every server runs them, possibly the same step at once.

docs.title: What a generated migration contains
docs.text:
MigrateAsync runs, in order: renames; property removals; Ensure… for each new or changed item (whole definition, keys included); property moves; group, tab and composition removals; whole-item deletions. Your hand-written code runs before the renames, so target a renamed item's old alias (and create any group it moved into that is new in this migration).

Anything Ferry cannot write safely becomes #error Review: … at the top of MigrateAsync, so the build fails until you handle it and delete the line. The item is then not restated; write its whole change yourself. This applies to:

  • an existing property's data type or variation;
  • a data type's editor or storage;
  • an existing type's variations;
  • a template's layout (master template);
  • a relation type's alias, what it relates, or its dependency flag;
  • aliases swapped or rotated between items, properties, groups or tabs;
  • a key changed under the same alias, or a container switched between group and tab.

A language's ISO code identifies it, so a code change is written as remove plus add; the removal refuses where a type varies by culture, so write it by hand there. Removals follow the stored-value rules and can fail on one environment but not another.

docs.title: Drift
docs.text:
Schema that differs from what the migrations produced (e.g. an edit on live) is drift, listed on the Advanced tab and by the health check across deploys until resolved. A migration that changes a drifted item does not clear it unless the result matches exactly. Resolve by either:

  • making the change on a development machine and choosing Create migration; or
  • choosing Accept current schema (administrator, any environment). The API can accept specific items; no or empty keys accepts everything. It returns the new status.
POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/ferry/schema/migrations/accept
{ "keys": ["<item key>", "..."] }

Development sites that write drafts show no drift (differences are the draft). Schema arriving by Ferry transfer is drift everywhere else, hence Ferry:Full:ContentOnly on receiving environments.

docs.title: Moving from a hand-written 0.5 plan
docs.text:
0.6 leaves your old MigrationPlan alone. To switch:

  1. Enable the settings on your development site and Create migration; with no history or plan file it is an adoption migration, marked applied locally.
  2. In the same commit, remove your old plan's registration.
  3. Deploy. Each environment runs the adoption migration once; matching schema is unchanged.

Ferry never reads or rewrites another plan's state.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
• ImageSharp advisory (GHSA-v76p-62qx-wwq2): Umbraco 17 depends on SixLabors.ImageSharp 3.1.x (heap out-of-bounds write, fixed in 3.2.0). Ferry doesn't reference it. 3.2.0 refuses Release builds without a Six Labors license key, so reference 3.2.0 if licensed, or record the advisory as accepted.
  • Environments on different migrations have different schema; content-only transfers between them are rejected with the items to deploy first.

docs.title: Extending Ferry
docs.text:
Ferry refuses what it does not understand: a property editor without a contract, or data a package keeps in its own tables, blocks the transfer with a message rather than being copied half-right. To teach Ferry about a package:

What the package adds What to do Section A property editor whose value has no ids, paths or references Declare it a scalar editor Scalar editors A property editor whose value points at pages, media or other items Register a value mapper (IFerryValueMapper) Mapped editors Data stored outside content (redirects, forms, settings rows, …) Write a Ferry package provider Package providers Media files of a type Ferry does not allow List the extension Media file types

Register everything the same way on every site that sends or receives it.

docs.title: Scalar editors
docs.text:
Scalar values are copied exactly as stored. Use only for values with no site-local ids, file paths or entity references (text, numbers, colours, a JSON settings object). A page or media key in a scalar value is copied without its dependency; use a mapped editor instead.

builder.AddFerryUmbracoFull(options => options.ScalarEditors.Add("Our.ColorPicker"));

or:

"Ferry": { "Editors": { "ScalarEditors": [ "Our.ColorPicker" ] } }

docs.title: Mapped editors
docs.text:
A value mapper returns the value to send and the value to store, and reports every page and media item the value points at, so they travel with the page and show in the review. Keys match on both sites after a transfer, so values storing keys or umb:// UDIs can usually be copied unchanged; the mapper's main job is reporting references. Ferry checks the round trip and declared references before saving.

Built-in mappers cover Umbraco's pickers, Multi URL Picker, rich text, Block List, Block Grid, Single Block, Contentment and MetaMomentum. For your own editor, implement IFerryValueMapper (Ferry.Umbraco.Values):

public sealed class LinkCardMapper : IFerryValueMapper
{
    public IReadOnlyCollection<string> Editors { get; } = ["Our.LinkCard"];

    // Keys are the same on both sites, so the stored value travels unchanged.
    public Task<string?> ToPortableAsync(object value, FerryValueContext context) => Task.FromResult(value?.ToString());
    public Task<object?> FromPortableAsync(string portable, FerryValueContext context) => Task.FromResult<object?>(portable);

    // Every page and media item the value points at.
    public Task<IReadOnlyCollection<GuidUdi>> ReferencesAsync(object value, FerryValueContext context) =>
        Task.FromResult<IReadOnlyCollection<GuidUdi>>(PageKeys(value?.ToString())
            .Select(key => new GuidUdi(Constants.UdiEntityType.Document, key)).ToArray());

    private static IEnumerable<Guid> PageKeys(string? value) => /* read the keys out of your stored JSON */ [];
}

Registering it also opts the editor in:

builder.AddFerryValueMapper<LinkCardMapper>();
  • FerryValueContext.Values maps nested values, such as a block's properties.
  • An alias in MappedEditors without a registered mapper is still refused.
  • Test on two disposable sites with different local ids: create content, Send it, and check a second review plans it as unchanged.

docs.title: Package providers
docs.text:
A package provider carries data a package keeps in its own tables (redirects, forms, banners, settings) in the same transfer as the pages and media it points at. Ferry ships two:

Package Provider What travels Skybrud.Umbraco.Redirects Ferry.Skybrud.Redirects, builder.AddFerrySkybrudRedirects() Redirects with their root page and destination page or media. Destination URLs must be site paths or http(s) URLs. Umbraco Forms Ferry.Umbraco.Forms, builder.AddFerryUmbracoForms() Form definitions with workflows and the page shown after submit. Form and theme pickers travel as plain values. Records, folders, prevalue sources and data sources are not transferred; a form using a prevalue or data source needs it on the destination first. 
builder.AddFerryUmbracoFull();
builder.AddFerrySkybrudRedirects();
builder.AddFerryUmbracoForms();

Forms workflows act on the server, so every workflow and field setting is checked: a view path must be a Razor view in the Forms email template folder (Forms/Emails/), and an address must be an http or https URL to a public host. A Save as an XML file workflow may only write xml, txt or csv files. Ferry checks the address as written; it cannot see what a host name resolves to when Umbraco Forms later calls it.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text:
Off by default, because providers write to tables Ferry otherwise leaves alone. Enable on both sites:

"Ferry": { "Full": { "AllowPackageItemTransfer": true } }

A site receiving items for a provider it lacks refuses the transfer before writing anything, naming the provider.

docs.title: What a transfer does
docs.text:
• Whole-site transfers carry every item of every provider.
  • Selected transfers carry items whose pages and media are all selected. Items pointing at nothing (e.g. a form with no after-submit page) travel only in whole-site transfers.
  • Items keep their key, show in the review as "ItemName: name" with changed fields, and are written after the pages and media they point at, in the same apply.
  • Items pointing at missing or recycled pages or media are left out of the export and logged.
  • Items are created or updated, never deleted.

docs.title: Writing a provider
docs.text:
Implement IFerryPackageProvider (Ferry.Umbraco.Packages):

Member What it does Alias Stable id: lowercase letters, digits, dashes, e.g. our-banners. Never change it. ItemName What one item is called in the review, e.g. Banner. ExportAllAsync Every item on this site. ExportAsync(key) One item or null; compared with the incoming item. ValidateAsync(item) Checks an incoming item before anything is written; throw InvalidOperationException or NotSupportedException with a message for the reviewer. ApplyAsync(item) Creates or updates the item, keeping its key.

Each item is a FerryPackageItem(Key, Name, Data, References):

  • Data: JSON object of portable settings. Omit local integer ids, dates and derived values so unchanged items compare equal. Property order does not matter.
  • References: pages (FerryReferenceKind.Document) and media (FerryReferenceKind.Media) the item needs, by key. They must exist on the destination or come in the same transfer.
public sealed class BannerProvider(IBannerService banners) : IFerryPackageProvider
{
    public string Alias => "our-banners";
    public string ItemName => "Banner";

    public Task<IReadOnlyList<FerryPackageItem>> ExportAllAsync(CancellationToken token) =>
        Task.FromResult<IReadOnlyList<FerryPackageItem>>(banners.GetAll().Select(ToItem).ToArray());

    public Task<FerryPackageItem?> ExportAsync(Guid key, CancellationToken token) =>
        Task.FromResult(banners.Get(key) is { } banner ? ToItem(banner) : null);

    public Task ValidateAsync(FerryPackageItem item, CancellationToken token) => Task.CompletedTask;

    public Task ApplyAsync(FerryPackageItem item, CancellationToken token)
    {
        var banner = banners.Get(item.Key) ?? new Banner { Key = item.Key };
        banner.Text = (string?)item.Data["text"] ?? "";
        banner.ImageKey = (string?)item.Data["image"] is { } image ? Guid.Parse(image) : null;
        banners.Save(banner);
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }

    private static FerryPackageItem ToItem(Banner banner) => new(
        banner.Key, banner.Text,
        new JsonObject { ["text"] = banner.Text, ["image"] = banner.ImageKey?.ToString("D") },
        banner.ImageKey is { } image ? [new(FerryReferenceKind.Media, image)] : []);
}

Register on both sites:

builder.AddFerryPackageProvider<BannerProvider>();

Guidelines:

  • Treat incoming data as untrusted. Validate every field in ValidateAsync and again in ApplyAsync: lengths, enums, and especially URLs (the Skybrud provider accepts only site paths and http(s) URLs).
  • Keep the key. If the package assigns random keys, set the source key after creating (the Skybrud provider updates its row in the apply's scope).
  • Map local ids. Store page keys in Data and look up the local id when applying.
  • Refuse clashes with a different local item (same URL or alias, other key) in ValidateAsync, naming both.
  • Limits: 256 KiB per item, 32 providers per site.

Reference implementation: SkybrudRedirectsProvider in src/Ferry.Skybrud.Redirects.

docs.title: Media file types
docs.text:
Ferry allows common image, document, audio, video and font types. Add others on both sites:

"Ferry": { "Full": { "AdditionalMediaExtensions": [ ".pdn" ] } }

Types a browser or server can run (.html, .js, .svgz, .cshtml, .exe and similar) are refused at startup.

docs.title: SQLite and large transfers
docs.text: On SQLite, Umbraco's relation tracking reads then writes after each save without a write lock, so a commit from another connection in between (e.g. Umbraco's background jobs, every few seconds) fails it with "database is locked" after minutes of retries. Ferry keeps its own background writes out of that gap. For a large first transfer into a SQLite site, set Umbraco:CMS:DistributedJobs:Delay to a few hours on the receiving site, or use SQL Server.
