docs.title: Ferry
docs.text:
Code-first schema and safe content deployment for Umbraco 17.

Ferry keeps schema in your code and moves content between sites, such as development, staging and live:

  • Code-first schema. SchemaBuilder declares data types, templates, media types and document types in Umbraco migrations, run once per environment. Keys derive from aliases, so schema is identical everywhere. An existing site can download its schema as one key-preserving migration. See code-first schema.
  • Generated migrations. Development backoffice schema edits become C# migrations you commit; other environments run them at startup and report drift. See generated migrations.
  • Content-only sites. With Ferry:Full:ContentOnly, a site rejects any transfer that would change its schema and lists what to deploy first.
  • Reviewed transfers. Send and Get (Push and Pull in the API) list every create, update and move and need an owner-bound approval before applying. Schema, media, references and blocks travel with the content.
  • Deployment workflow. Per-user queue, offline .ferry.zip packages, import at startup, snapshots and restore points, user-group permissions for delegated editors.
  • Extensible. Custom property editors and package data (Skybrud redirects, Umbraco Forms, your own package) can join transfers. See extending Ferry.
  • Safe on real sites. One operation at a time across load-balanced instances (database lease). Indexing and caches pause during large imports. Each apply writes a recovery journal.

Documentation: https://imkeuri.github.io/ferry-umbraco/. Ferry needs no other synchronisation tool or file export.

Free to use, closed source. Free for any site, including commercial work, under the Ferry Freeware License.

Status: experimental, pre-1.0. Tested on Umbraco 17.6.2 and .NET 10. See supported scope.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
dotnet add package Ferry.Umbraco --prerelease
dotnet add package Ferry.Backoffice --prerelease

builder.CreateUmbracoBuilder()
    .AddBackOffice()
    .AddWebsite()
    .AddComposers()
    .AddFerryUmbracoFull()
    .Build();

Configuration goes in a Ferry section of appsettings.json; see Host integration.

docs.title: Using the backoffice
docs.text:
Ferry.Backoffice adds a Ferry workspace under Settings › Synchronisation:

Tab Use Overview Connected sites, Send to another site, Get from another site (whole site or chosen pages), recent activity. Connect your first site when none is connected. Sites This site (name, address, role), Connected sites (one row per site: what each may do, status, edit, disconnect), Connect a site (paste a pairing code) and Let another site connect (create pairing codes). Packages Export a .ferry.zip (chosen pages and media, or whole site), import one by dropping it on the page, create or restore snapshots. Advanced Publish on another site; danger zone with Move to recycle bin on another site and Seed another site.

Sites. This site shows its name, address and role (Development, Staging, Live or Other); other sites see the role next to its name. Set Ferry:Backoffice:SiteRole to fix the role in configuration; the card then reads Set in configuration. A configured destination can declare its own role with Ferry:Backoffice:Destinations:<id>:Role.

Connected sites has one row per site, joining the connection this site makes to it and the access key it uses to call this one, matched by address. Columns: Site (role badge, Managed in config), Address, We may and They may (Send, Get, Publish and Compare chips) and Status (online, unreachable with the reason, or not checked, with Check again). Edit changes the name, role, whether we may Get, and what they may do here. Disconnect stops this site connecting and revokes their key; Edit also has Revoke their access and Stop connecting separately. A site managed in configuration can only have their key revoked, not its connection removed here. A site test also reports whether the other site lets this one publish.

Pairing. Let another site connect creates a pairing code: name the other site, choose what it may do here (Compare is implied by Send or Get) and optionally tick Allow two-way. The code is shown once, with Copy. The codes table lists each as Waiting (hours left), Used by or Expired, with Revoke or Remove; used and expired codes are kept for 30 days. On site B, Connect a site and paste the code: Ferry reads it as you paste and shows the site, what it allows, whether it is two-way and the hours left, or says why it cannot be used (older Ferry code, expired, already used, not valid, or this site's own code). When A allowed two-way, B's admin picks what A may do on B, edits this site's address if A should call a different one, and both connections are made in the same step; choose the new site's role there too. A code works once and expires after 24 hours; it is not the access key itself. Codes from Ferry 0.7 (ferry1.…) are refused. No pairing code? connects with an address and an access key (Create an access key instead). Other sites label this one with Ferry:Backoffice:SiteName when set, otherwise with its host (for example staging.example.com).

Content tree Actions offer Send to…, Get from…, Add to queue and (administrators) Publish on another site…. Each opens a panel with three steps:

  1. Choose. Pick the site (cards show whether it can be reached), what to send, the version (latest draft or published), the languages, and the options: send or get in the background, allow moves, publish after sending. Every option says in a line what it does.
  2. Review. Tiles count what will be created, updated or moved ("4 new pages, 1 updated page"). Schema changes are shown as a change table of what differs, and notes, moves and template warnings are always visible, never behind a toggle. Nothing changes until you send.
  3. Done. The result, with links to open the items on the other site. After a Get, Undo this get restores the restore point taken before it.

While a site is checked or a review is prepared the panel shows placeholders, a send shows its progress (and batch, for large sends), a failure shows the reason with Try again, and with no sites connected it points to connecting one. The queue's Ready to send tab offers the same version and language choices (when it holds pages) and the same option switches as a single transfer, then the same Review and Done steps. Administrators also get Send everything to… and Get everything from… on the Content and Media section roots: every top-level item with its descendants (Content brings its dependencies and referenced media as usual; Media sends only the media library), through the same review, background option and batches. Items arrive as drafts. Administrators sending Content to a site that supports publication can tick Publish on after sending: the review button becomes Send and publish, and after the send the selected items (and their child items, never items pulled in as dependencies) are published in the sent cultures. If the publication check finds a problem, such as an unpublished parent there, the drafts stay and the publication review opens instead. Not available for background sends. The top-bar Ferry button opens the queue (send all or download as a package) and recent activity. The Send with Ferry and Get with Ferry group permissions control access, on top of delegated-editor grants.

docs.title: Supported and limits
docs.text:
Supported: invariant Content, Content variants and segments, selected MediaPicker3 references, segment-varying scalar Media values, Content UploadField assets (draft with hash and byte checks; published as immutable publish-time snapshots, failing closed when the snapshot is missing, corrupt or mismatched). Each capability and its limits are listed in the supported scope.

Limits:

  • Not yet covered: arbitrary UploadField/editor configurations, multi-node hosting, cross-browser, accessibility and production topologies.
  • Unsupported: unknown/custom editors, user/member references. Not every Umbraco editor is supported.
  • Templates must already exist at the destination; schema changes needing storage migration are blocked.
  • Jobs and approvals are process-local; multi-node needs affinity and external coordination.

docs.title: Transfer model
docs.text:
• Stable GUID identities across sites; local numeric IDs may differ.
  • Create/update/unchanged previews, dependency ordering, cyclic soft references.
  • Whole-site or selected-tree transfer with prerequisite/reference closure (Full mode reads only that closure).
  • Optional culture scope (Full mode): selected variants plus invariant values; other destination variants untouched. Bound into the approval; peers without the capability are rejected. New scoped content needs the default and mandatory cultures.
  • Approvals are bound to source and destination fingerprints: edits to incoming entities or prerequisites need a fresh preview, unrelated edits do not.
  • Peers negotiate a versioned, authenticated capability declaration first; incompatible formats fail closed.
  • Native draft saves, whatever the source publication state.
  • Media is verified by SHA256 and length. An optional probe skips bytes the peer already has.
  • Culture-varying Media (Full mode). Umbraco 17.6.2 drops Media culture names on read, so Ferry keeps them in its own table; native APIs and the backoffice do not show them after a restart.
  • Administrator pull, and optional metadata-only Browse and name-only BrowseSearch.
  • Destination-only entities are kept. No implicit deletion or rollback.
  • On failure, completed and possibly touched entities are reported separately.

Adapters:

  • AddFerryUmbraco(): invariant TextBox/TextArea drafts on matching preinstalled schemas.
  • AddFerryUmbracoFull(): writes through Umbraco's services, so other packages' save handlers run. Requires an ISyncAssetStore. Editor/storage changes to existing shared data types are blocked. Re-export older experimental manifests.

The BackOffice package has its own composer, independent of the transport switch and adapter.

docs.title: Host integration
docs.text:
Register the adapter, then configure transport explicitly:

builder.Services.AddFerryTransport(new SyncTransportOptions
{
    BearerToken = tokenFromYourSecretProvider
});
builder.Services.AddFerryFileAssets(privateAssetDirectory);
builder.Services.AddFerryFileRecovery(privateRecoveryDirectory);
// After building/configuring the Umbraco application:
app.MapFerry();

For named peers with per-operation permissions, use the reload-aware registration:

builder.Configuration.AddEnvironmentVariables(); // or the host's managed secret provider
builder.Services.AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration(
    builder.Configuration.GetRequiredSection("Ferry"));

Set peer identity, revision and permitted operations in Ferry:Peers (Compare, read-only item inventories, is implied for peers that may Preview or Export), with tokens from the secret provider (for example Ferry__Peers__0__Tokens__0). See the peer-policy contract.

  • Bearer secrets: random, at least 32 characters. No defaults are provided.
  • Keep asset and recovery storage outside public static-file directories.
  • In the sample, endpoints are off by default and Ferry:Mode is DraftText (default) or Full.

docs.title: Access keys from the backoffice only
docs.text:
Access keys from Settings › Ferry › Sites (made when a pairing code is used, or created directly; each shows as a row in Connected sites) are also receiver credentials. A receiver using only those needs no token or placeholder peer: AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration (or AddFerryTransport) accepts an empty Ferry section when an ISyncManagedPeerSource is registered. With neither, the host refuses to start.

Pairing codes are redeemed at POST /ferry/v1/pairing/claim, mapped by MapFerry(). It is the one route without a bearer token (the single-use code is the credential): HTTPS only, 8 KiB bodies, and at most 10 attempts per client address and 60 overall per minute on each instance. A gateway in front must let it through like the rest of /ferry/v1. For two-way codes, the issuing site calls the other site's /ferry/v1/capabilities before saving the connection, so it must be able to reach that address.

docs.title: Getting past host authentication
docs.text: /ferry/v1 does its own authentication. Basic auth or an IP/SSO gateway in front will block it. For Umbraco basic auth, add the shared-secret header (Umbraco:CMS:BasicAuth:SharedSecret) to requests on that path before UseUmbraco(); otherwise exclude the path in the gateway.

docs.title: TLS terminated by a proxy
docs.text:
The receiver rejects plain HTTP. When TLS ends at a proxy (Azure Container Apps, App Service, Front Door, nginx), forward the scheme:

builder.Services.Configure<ForwardedHeadersOptions>(options =>
{
    options.ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto;
    options.KnownIPNetworks.Clear(); // only when the ingress is the sole way in; otherwise list its network
    options.KnownProxies.Clear();
});
// First in the pipeline:
app.UseForwardedHeaders();

docs.title: Where state is kept
docs.text:
State Storage Survives redeploy / new replica? Servers, access keys and pairing codes cmsFerryServer, cmsFerryAccessKey, cmsFerryPairingInvitation (token hashes only) Yes. Secrets in those rows ASP.NET Data Protection Only with a persisted, shared key ring (e.g. PersistKeysToAzureBlobStorage); otherwise keys stop working after a redeploy and a warning is logged. Peer cache Memory, 30 seconds Revoked keys stop working on other instances within 30 seconds. Operation history, submissions, snapshots, restore points cmsFerryOperation, cmsFerrySubmission, cmsFerrySnapshot Yes. Previews and batch sessions Memory No. See Hosting requirements. Receiver approvals (push, publication, tree trash) Memory, per process No. See Hosting requirements. Staged assets, recovery records Directories given to AddFerryFileAssets / AddFerryFileRecovery Only on persistent storage.

cmsFerry* tables are created whenever the packages are installed, even with Ferry:Enabled or Ferry:Backoffice:Enabled false. To remove Ferry: uninstall the packages, drop the cmsFerry* tables, and delete umbracoKeyValue rows whose key starts with Ferry. or Umbraco.Core.Upgrader.State+Ferry..

docs.title: Hosting requirements
docs.text:
Database. Use SQL Server for production receivers. On SQLite with the default Cache=Shared, a burst of writes (such as a large apply) can deadlock Umbraco's cache write with its background jobs, and every later request hangs. If you must use SQLite, set Cache=Private.

One warm instance. Previews (15 minutes, single-use), batched push sessions (4 hours) and receiver approvals live in memory and are lost on restart, scale-to-zero or a different instance. Both sites must run one warm instance:

  • Azure Container Apps: minimum and maximum replicas 1.
  • App Service and other load-balanced hosts: one instance, or session affinity for the source backoffice. The receiver must be a single instance; site-to-site calls carry no affinity cookie.

Otherwise apply returns 410 Gone ("This preview has expired") and changes nothing.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
Endpoints under /ferry/v1 require HTTPS and bearer authentication, except POST /pairing/claim (see Access keys from the backoffice only); responses are not cached.

Endpoint Purpose GET /capabilities Peer protocol, adapter, entity, operation and limit support GET /manifest Export the complete supported snapshot POST /export Export selected roots, descendants and dependencies POST /browse One metadata-only page of Content or Media children (if Browse is registered) POST /browse/search One metadata-only name-search page (if BrowseSearch is granted) POST /preview Validate a manifest, return a plan POST /apply Revalidate the approved fingerprint and apply GET /assets/{hash} Stream an asset PUT /assets/{hash}?length=... Verify and stage an asset GET /operations List recovery operation summaries (if registered) GET /operations/{id} Operation outcome GET /operations/{id}/recovery Before-state recovery record POST /publication/preview Validate destination keys and cultures POST /publication/apply Publish only the approved selection

HTTP 200 does not mean success: check SyncPlan.IsValid and ExecutionResult.Status. Errors: 401 authentication, 400 malformed, 413 oversized, 422 adapter capability. JSON requests default to 8 MiB; assets have a separate limit.

SyncRemoteClient calls one fixed HTTPS destination. SyncTransferClient.PrepareAsync() negotiates, exports, stages assets and previews; ApplyAsync() is separate and rechecks the peer. Redirects are disabled. Configure only trusted peers.

docs.title: Administrator pull
docs.text:
Requires AllowPull: true on the server-side connection. Endpoints under /umbraco/management/api/v1/ferry/pull:

Endpoint Behaviour POST /preview Full site or 1–1000 typed roots; returns an owner-bound, expiring approval. POST /{id}/apply Consumes the approval, rechecks connection and capabilities, applies the frozen manifest with recovery journal. Never publishes, deletes, schedules or re-exports. POST /browse Content or Media, optional parent key, page size 1–100. Returns key, name, breadcrumb (last 16 ancestors, … if truncated), child presence, cultures. Never properties, entities, snapshots or bytes. POST /browse/search Name term 2–128 characters, no %, _ or [; up to 50 per page, offset up to 10,000. Names only.

Browse and search need source Browse and Export and local Preview and Apply; a source can grant Browse alone. BrowseSearch is opt-in (GET /capabilities?extensions=browse-search). Content (not Media) can be scoped by culture; see transfer model. Delegated Pull is draft-only, for granted groups within permitted roots, cultures and Umbraco permissions.

docs.title: Delegated editor Push
docs.text:
Administrators can grant a user group a limited Push to one destination:

{
  "Ferry": {
    "Backoffice": {
      "DelegatedEditors": [
        {
          "GroupAlias": "editors",
          "Direction": "Push",
          "ConnectionId": "Production",
          "ContentRootKeys": ["11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"],
          "MediaRootKeys": ["22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"],
          "RemoteContentRootKeys": [],
          "RemoteMediaRootKeys": [],
          "AllowedCultures": ["en-US"]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
  • GroupAlias: the stored group alias, not the display name. ConnectionId: the configured destination key.
  • ContentRootKeys / MediaRootKeys: roots members may send. AllowedCultures: variant values sent.
  • Native Read permission is also required; grant and scope are rechecked at preview and apply. Anything missing, invalid or non-matching denies access.

Push preview takes legacy contentRoots or roots: [{ kind: "Content" | "Media", key }]: one of them, with 1–1000 unique keys, or an empty contentRoots for the whole site. Both sites must support every selected kind.

docs.title: Operational boundaries
docs.text:
• Credentials. The legacy bearer credential grants every operation; named peers can be limited and rotated, and reload with configuration (limits need a restart). Treat every receiver credential as an administrative secret.
  • Concurrency. Fingerprints detect changes; they do not lock editors or replace authorization. The receiver serializes requests per process; external edits and multi-node writers need extra coordination.
  • Recovery. With the Full adapter, each apply is all-or-nothing on the receiving site: a cancelling handler, failed validation or error rolls back the whole batch, including media and view files. Saved/Published handlers run after commit; if one fails, the batch stays saved and Ferry shows a warning naming it. A push over 250 items is split into batches, and each batch is atomic on its own. Records keep before-state and known outcomes; no outcome record means completion is unknown. Recovery data contains site content; protect it.
  • Live impact. Drafts are not published, but schema, media, hierarchy and sort changes can affect the live site.
  • Out of scope: executable templates/scripts, account replication.

See integration decisions, supported scope and recovery limits and third-party notices.

docs.title: Help and feedback
docs.text:
• Bugs: open an issue with Ferry and Umbraco versions, database and steps. Remove tokens, connection strings and passwords.
  • Questions and ideas: Discussions.
  • Package or editor support: use the Package or editor support issue form, or see extending Ferry.
  • Security problems: report privately, never in a public issue.

docs.title: Supported scope
docs.text:
Tested baseline: Umbraco 17.6.2 on .NET 10; the package name does not imply support for another major.

Supported between two sites: invariant draft text, hierarchy and stable identities; draft changes to live content; missing document/data types and compositions; language creation and en-US/fr-FR values; rich-text local links and embedded images (with native legacy-link normalization); reciprocal content pickers; nested Block List content/settings and schema closure; selected subtrees with referenced entities; repeat imports without changes or duplicates; default and named-segment values; existing template assignments (template files and hierarchies are not transferred); explicit culture publication and mandatory-language protection. Scheduled destination and schema identity conflicts reject before writes.

Capability Limits Image media, new media types, scalar metadata, MediaPicker3 references Full mode; picker identities map to destination Media keys Segment-varying scalar Media Full mode: TextBox, invariant values, case-varied segment identities, unchanged replay Culture-varying Media names, captions, files Distinct en-US/fr-FR captions and bytes, names kept in Ferry's durable store, repeat Unchanged. Umbraco 17.6.2 returns native culture names as null on a fresh read, so the Backoffice does not show them. Content UploadField See exclusions Block Grid, Multinode Treepicker, Multi URL Picker Documents in Block Grid blocks (with element and data types), MNTP documents/media, Multi URL Picker document/media links. Values identical; media link url is the destination path; external links kept; repeat Unchanged. Block Grid areas, nested grids, a grid inside a block property and Single Block values are deep-equal (tests/e2e/nested-tags.spec.ts). Single Block element types are not followed as references in this release: send them with the schema. Full-site Dictionary Items Keeps GUID identity, hierarchy, translations, language dependencies. No moves or deletion; deleting a destination translation rejects. Opt-in dictionary-item capability (older peers reject). Audit identity Umbraco SuperUserKey. Scoped destination preview/apply, recovery before-state — Tree moves / tree trash See below Published source version; culture-scoped transfer See below Administrator preview/apply and approval ownership — Peer capabilities, Full/Draft format rejection — Named receiver peers, reload fail-closed, approval envelopes See named receiver policies Administrator draft pull See administrator pull Update field comparison Bounded Content/Media differences in admin previews; only known scalar editors show values; receiver preview needs a current Export grant for target values Schema differences in the review Changed schema items (document, media and data types, templates) appear in the review as a change table of what differs, not only as a count; the review also notes that every page using them changes too. Typed Media push Destination kind preflight before export Settings dashboard, transfer, publication, history Layout, accessibility, cross-browser and production topology untested. Delegated editor Push One connection; exact group alias; local roots; allowed cultures; native Read; Ferry.Push (permissions). No verb: 403. Delegated editor Pull Explicit grant, existing local root, permitted remote root/culture, native permission, Ferry.Pull on updated items and create parents. Draft-only; no full-site or schema changes.

No commercial parity is claimed. Ferry is standalone; its Backoffice is at Settings → Synchronisation → Ferry. Full transfer saves through Umbraco's native services, so other packages' save handlers fire normally. Schema and media changes go to live definitions and files; publishing content is separate, unless an administrator ticks Publish on after sending, which runs the normal publication review and apply after the send and stops at the review when it reports errors. Back up the site and database before using it on a real site.

docs.title: Selected transfers and operational limits
docs.text:
Scoped planning. Full mode implements IScopedSyncExportStore (a root selection resolves its source closure before serializing or opening media) and IScopedSyncDestinationStore (preview/apply reads only closure entities and external direct prerequisites). Other adapters use full snapshots. A Language root lookup by portable key may enumerate serializer-derived language identities.

  • Approval fingerprints that snapshot: edits to incoming entities or their prerequisites invalidate it; unrelated edits do not.
  • Schema alias collisions and shared-schema checks run at preview and apply; invalid closure entities reject the transfer.
  • The closure includes ancestors, schemas and referenced entities, which may be updated. Review the whole plan.
  • Recovery records use the same snapshot.

Asset availability. An authenticated, bounded probe reports whether a peer already staged an asset's hash and length, so Push, Pull and typed clients skip repeat network bytes. Older peers and cache eviction fall back to full transfer. Descriptors stay in the manifest, fingerprint and recovery records. Target media is still exported and staged locally (avoiding that is roadmap work).

Culture scope (optional). Limits Content variant transfer to selected cultures, frozen in the manifest and fingerprint. Selected names/values and invariant values transfer; other destination variants are kept. Pull peers without the capability are rejected before export. Creating a scoped item needs the default and mandatory cultures. The Content modal's culture input defaults to all; Media has no scope.

Published source version (optional; Draft is default). The source's PublishedCultures set the scope; each transfers its name, template and published value per segment. Other destination drafts are kept. Selecting an unpublished culture rejects. A full-site export, or a tree selected with its descendants, omits pages with no published version (never published, or unpublished since) and the preview names them in a note; a page selected on its own without one is refused by name, and a published page below an omitted one fails, naming both. Results land as destination drafts. Peers without the capability reject.

Tree moves. Set allowMoves: true on a Push or Pull preview (default false; a toggle in the transfer modals and Settings dashboard). The destination must enable Ferry:Full:AllowExistingTreeMoves and advertise existing-tree-move. Preview shows old/new paths, descendant count, publication impact and field changes; approval freezes the subtree and publication state, and stale approval rejects. The move carries destination-only descendants and may affect a published path, but never publishes. Administrators only; no deletion.

Tree trash. A separate receiver-only administrator operation; omitting an item from a transfer never trashes it.

  • Requires Ferry:Full:AllowExistingTreeTrash (default false) and separate TrashPreview/TrashApply peer operations. No other grant, including delegated ones, permits trash.
  • 1–100 unique, non-overlapping roots. Recycled or top-level roots, and Content with a publication schedule in the branch, reject.
  • Preview shows paths, descendant and published-descendant counts. The 15-minute, owner-bound, single-use approval freezes branch, ancestors and publication state; any change rejects as stale.
  • Apply uses the native recycle bin and never empties it. The before-state is journaled under a returned operation ID for manual recovery; there is no rollback or restore of published versions or files. Check the recycle bin and journal before retrying an unknown outcome.

Capabilities. Peers publish an authenticated, no-store declaration (protocol/schema version, adapter, kinds, operations, limits), checked before export or staging and again before apply. Full and DraftText formats are incompatible. Publication has its own operations and approval.

Boundary Limit JSON requests 8 MiB default, up to 64 MiB Backoffice frozen manifest 8 MiB Typed client manifest/JSON response 16 MiB Typed client request timeout Two minutes Adapter media export 100 MiB per file, regardless of transport limits Recovery journal (optional) 64 MiB per record default; each apply is atomic; recovery records outcomes Durable job store (optional) 16 jobs (1–64), 64 MiB records (1–512, not below the JSON limit), 1,000 terminal records (1–1,000); admission timeout 30 s (1–120)

Each transfer builds one whole manifest: no paged protocol, resumable upload or background continuation. These are not tested large-site capacity figures.

Handlers on the receiving site. With the Full adapter (AddFerryUmbracoFull), each apply batch runs in one Umbraco scope that also covers the media, view, partial, stylesheet and script file systems. The DraftText adapter still writes item by item and keeps the items written before a failure. - A veto rolls the whole batch back: a cancelled Saving, Publishing or Moving notification, failed validation, or any error. The result says nothing from the batch was kept and carries the handler's message. - Saved and Published handlers run once per batch, after the commit, as Umbraco runs them. If one throws, the batch stays saved and the result is Completed with a warning naming the failure. The handlers queued after it did not run; Ferry refreshes the published cache and search index for the batch, but cannot replay webhooks or other site handlers. - A push is split into batches of up to 250 counted items; a Pull, package import or restore applies its whole manifest in one transaction. Above Ferry:Backoffice:LargeApplyWarningItems (default 1,000 written items; Unchanged and schema items do not count) the preview warns that editors on that site cannot save while it runs, and the review asks for confirmation. While a batch runs: on SQL Server, backoffice reads time out after 60 s and writes after 5 s; on SQLite the database is write-locked. Measured in tests/e2e/nested-tags.spec.ts on a developer machine: a 250-image media batch applies in about 13–18 s on SQL Server 2025 and 2–3 s on SQLite; a backoffice media save on the target during the SQL Server batch failed after 5 s ("Lock request time out period exceeded"), and the batch completed. - An apply refuses to start inside an open Umbraco scope, and reports another file-scoped operation as retryable. - On SQLite the batch holds the database write lock, so the background operation-lease renewal cannot write while it runs; the batch renews the lease itself between its entities, inside its own transaction, so a long batch does not let it expire, and renews it once more after the batch, outside it, because what it wrote inside is lost if the batch rolls back. On SQL Server the lease table is not locked by the batch, and the background renewal continues as usual.

docs.title: Durable Push and local Pull
docs.text:
• Push: offered at review when the destination advertises durable-transfer-jobs for its Apply peer (only with its private job store and journal). Rechecks capability, configuration and access before one admission POST. Not for delegated Push or publication.
  • Local Pull (EnableDurableLocalPull): LocalPull job kind with its own owner binding. At admission and execution it rechecks source, credential fingerprint, grant and native permissions, and preflights staged Media (100 MiB each, read via verified streams). Bearer tokens are never stored.
  • Both: owner-bound idempotency (same request returns the original receipt; a changed one conflicts), refreshable receipt and status, a browser recovery key, and work continues after the browser stops waiting.
  • Lost responses, interruptions or restarts give OutcomeUnknown; inspect before retrying. No automatic retry, rollback, cancel or replay. Single-process queue.

docs.title: Named receiver policies
docs.text:
A receiver uses one optional legacy bearer token (all operations) or named peers with id, rotation tokens, enabled flag, revision and an allow-list of: capabilities, export, preview, apply, asset read/write, publication preview/apply, recovery read, browse, BrowseSearch (advertised only on request), compare. Named peers scope the machine credential only, not user groups, roots or cultures.

Compare. A read-only peer permission for item inventories (identity, name, state; no payloads). Access keys that allow Send or Get imply it, as do configured peers with Preview or Export; it is not part of the policy hash, so upgrading never invalidates existing approvals or durable jobs. Nothing uses it yet; the compare view arrives in a later release.

Sites and roles. Settings › Ferry › Sites shows each connected site once, joining our outbound connection and their access key by address, with what each side may do (Send, Get, Publish, Compare). A site has a role (Development, Staging, Live or Other): this site's from the backoffice or Ferry:Backoffice:SiteRole, a configured destination's from Ferry:Backoffice:Destinations:<id>:Role. Roles are labels; they grant nothing. Connections and connections defined in configuration are shown as Managed in config and cannot be edited or removed there. Inbound configured peers (Ferry:Peers) do not appear in the Sites table. A configured site that has a matching managed access key can still have that key edited or revoked. Saving a key's permissions unchanged keeps its revision (so approvals and durable jobs stay valid); a real change takes effect on other instances within the peer cache lifetime (about 30 s).

AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration re-reads policy per request after a reload; invalid policy fails closed. Request and asset limits are startup settings. Bump the revision on every change. Approvals are HMAC-protected, process-local and expire in 15 minutes; restarts, scale-to-zero or other instances invalidate them (410 Gone), so run one receiver instance. They are not a replay ledger. See the peer-policy contract.

docs.title: User-group permissions for delegated editors
docs.text: Two verbs, Send with Ferry (Ferry.Push) and Receive with Ferry (Ferry.Pull), are assigned in Users per document or as a group default (media always uses the default). Delegated editors need the verb plus their grant and native permissions; administrators are exempt. Ferry:Backoffice:RequireGranularPermissions (default true) disables the check. The first start after upgrading gives each DelegatedEditors group its verb once; later groups need it assigned manually.

docs.title: Administrator pull
docs.text:
Requires a connection with AllowPull true. Preview takes the full site or 1–1000 roots, stages verified assets and freezes an owner-bound 15-minute approval. Apply rechecks state and writes drafts via the recovery journal; it never publishes, deletes, schedules or queues a durable job.

Browse needs an HTTPS source and pull preflight (source Browse and Export, local Preview and Apply, matching format and kind); a peer may be granted Browse alone. It pages configured roots (1–100 items: key, name, breadcrumb, child flag, cultures), using one ancestor lookup per page (last 16 IDs; ellipsis when truncated). No integer paths, properties, payloads or media bytes. Ordered by sortOrder without guarantees for ties or concurrent changes; 3 MiB response ceiling. Delegated navigation verifies ancestry and each child.

BrowseSearch applies the same checks and searches names only: 2–128 characters, %, _ and [ rejected, 50 per page, offset up to 10,000.

Delegated previews hide field differences. Delegated Pull grants scope roots and cultures and cannot request full-site or schema changes. Experimental; not production-ready.

docs.title: Explicit exclusions and fail-closed behavior
docs.text:
Untested values reject before writes:

  • Culture-varying Media beyond the tested name/caption/umbracoFile shape; segment-varying Media beyond TextBox.
  • Published-source UploadField without a matching immutable publish-time snapshot (PublishedVersionId, property/culture/segment, raw value); missing, corrupt, preexisting or mismatched snapshots fail closed. New SaveAndPublish content is captured before the version exists and bound afterwards; an en-US-only republish carries the fr-FR snapshot forward. SQL Server stores them in cmsFerryPublishedContentAsset. Draft-source uses hash-addressed descriptors with byte checks. Untested: other culture-varying UploadField setups, other file editors, multi-node hosting, production topology.
  • Relational Media editors other than MediaPicker3.
  • Custom editors without a registered contract (below).
  • User and Member references and arbitrary relation types.
  • Template files and hierarchies, unless both peers enable executable templates; otherwise the template must exist at the destination.
  • Schema migrations: storage/variation changes, property or composition removal.

docs.title: Optional modules
docs.text:
Off unless stated. Any transfer opt-in moves a site to protocol/schema 2 (Full format v6), which negotiates only with v6 peers and needs the capability on both; default sites stay on protocol 1 (Full format v5).

Module Enable Contract and limits Executable templates Ferry:Full:AllowTemplateTransfer, both peers Create-only Razor as SHA-256 assets (1 MiB each; 16 MiB/200 per manifest). Aliases [A-Za-z0-9_]; _ViewStart/_ViewImports blocked; alias/key, duplicate and existing Views/*.cshtml collisions reject (fails closed without a content root). Parents first; a stored alias or Layout parent differing from the approval is removed. Shows an executable-code warning. No updates, renames, deletions; rendering unproven. People Ferry:Full:AllowPeopleTransfer, both peers Full-site. User groups (sections, fallback and document permissions, languages, start nodes), users (groups, start nodes, language), member groups/types, members (identity, approval on create, groups, invariant text/textarea/email/integer/decimal/true-false/date values). Never administrators, their group, the super-user or API users. No passwords, security stamps, lockout, login state or tokens; reset passwords. Collisions on name/alias/user name/email reject; other editors and permission types fail closed; max 10,000 members. Domains Ferry:Full:AllowDomainTransfer, both peers Default culture and ordered hostnames travel with the node. Taken or duplicated hostnames, wildcard/unsafe names and non-BCP-47 cultures reject. Apply replaces the node's set; no domains never clears. Offline packages Administrators .ferry.zip: header (capabilities, manifest) plus assets/<sha256> blobs. Rejects unexpected names, traversal, duplicates, undeclared/missing blobs, entries over MaximumPackageBytes (256 MiB), unsupported versions, hash mismatches (even cached). Pull planner, one-time approval, journal; never publishes. No commercial format compatibility. Startup import Ferry:Backoffice:ImportOnStartup:Enabled, Files (default umbraco/Ferry/import-on-startup.ferry.zip, relative to the content root) Validated like an upload, applied under one gate hold with journal, restore point and history (actor startup) before the site reports started. Errors block apply; never publishes. File renamed .imported/.failed with a .result.json, so it never runs twice; other instances plan it unchanged. Snapshots and restore points Administrators; CreateRestorePoints on by default Snapshots (full site or roots) in cmsFerrySnapshot, shared by instances; compare or restore. Restore points capture every touched entity before each local apply (import, restore, Pull, received Push, durable); capture failure aborts (409). Restores write drafts; they do not delete newer entities, restore published versions, files, secrets or infrastructure. MaximumSnapshots (50) evicts oldest restore points, never manual snapshots. Relations Ferry:Full:AllowRelationTransfer, both peers Full-site. Custom Document/Media relation types and relations; never system types. Identity is (type, parent, child); added or comment-updated, never deleted. Alias/object-type collisions reject. Document blueprints Ferry:Full:AllowBlueprintTransfer, both peers Full-site, full content pipeline; folders not transferred (blueprints land at root). Bulk apply suspensions On; Ferry:Full:BulkApply:Suspensions (None, ScheduledPublishing, Examine, DocumentCache, All), MinimumOperations (50) Large batches pause scheduled publishing, Examine and document cache via Suspendable, resuming on every exit. Resuming Examine rebuilds all indexes, hence the threshold. Overlaps are reference-counted; failed resumes are logged. Process-local. Send or get everything Administrators; Send everything to… / Get everything from… on the Content and Media section roots Selects every top-level item of that tree (up to 1000) with descendants, never the whole site. Send reads this site's tree; Get asks the source for its top-level items at review. Oversized sends split into batches as usual; Get is one review (use Get in the background for large trees). An empty tree shows Nothing to send. Transfer queue Users with Ferry access; GET/PUT ferry/queue Up to 1000 roots per user in cmsFerryQueue, across browsers; cleared after transfer. Older browser queues upload once; servers without the endpoint keep browser-only queues. Trees show "Queued for transfer". Grants nothing. Content-only sites Ferry:Full:ContentOnly, receiver Rejects any transfer or import that would create, update or move document/media/member types, data types, languages, templates, media-type variations or relation types, listing up to 20 (kind, alias, key). Unchanged schema is fine. Items breaking root/child rules are placed as at the source when its type is in the transfer. Checked at review and apply. Dictionary and members unaffected. Code-first schema (SchemaBuilder) Your migrations; see code-first schema Ensure… creates or converges data types, templates, languages, media and document types; never removes, refuses destructive changes. Keys are RFC 4122 v5 UUIDs from aliases. Remove…Async (refused with stored values unless allowDataLoss: true), Rename…Async, MovePropertyAsync. GET …/ferry/schema/code exports a key-preserving migration. Generated migrations Ferry:Schema:Migrations:Enabled; WriteDrafts, ProjectPath on dev; see generated migrations Create migration writes a timestamped migration and plan file (first adopts the schema). Pending ones run at startup in order; a failure rolls back with its views, blocks later ones and shows on the Advanced tab and a health check. Drift listed until resolved or Accept current schema. No member types. Package data Ferry:Full:AllowPackageItemTransfer and a provider on both peers (AddFerrySkybrudRedirects(), AddFerryUmbracoForms(), AddFerryPackageProvider<T>()) Keyed PackageItem entities. Full-site carries all; selected carries items whose pages/media are all selected; items pointing at missing/binned content are skipped and logged. Never deleted. Missing providers refuse before writes. Skybrud: site paths or http(s) only. Forms: definitions and workflows only; forms missing a prevalue/data source at the destination are refused. See extending Ferry. Site seed Administrators seed/preflight reports compatibility, emptiness (with Browse) and shared features; the seed is a full-site Push review, so reruns apply remaining differences.

docs.title: Schema storage and migrations
docs.text: Data type exports carry native storage metadata, which apply keeps. Changing a data type's editor or storage, or changing or removing a property, is blocked unless Umbraco reports no stored values (element-type use always counts). Composition removal and other migrations need explicit code. Re-export older manifests without storage metadata. For schema deployed with code, use Ferry:Full:ContentOnly.

docs.title: Custom property editors
docs.text:
Unknown custom editors fail closed. Declare verified behavior explicitly:

umbraco.AddFerryUmbracoFull(options =>
{
    options.ScalarEditors.Add("Custom.PlainText");
    options.MappedEditors.Add("Custom.Relations");
});

Scalar contracts are only for values without site-local IDs, file paths or entity references. Mapped contracts need an installed value mapper (declaring the alias does not create one); round trips and references are checked before saving. Test on two sites with different local IDs.

docs.title: Explicit publication
docs.text:
Select destination keys and cultures, get a fresh preview, then apply with its fingerprint. A sole * means all available cultures (and invariant content). Unpublished ancestors must be selected or published first; invariant children of an unpublished variant ancestor need it published first. Schedules are separate.

Properties, draft, schema, ancestor and language state are validated. Missing mandatory cultures are never added silently. It never infers source publication, publishes unselected ancestors, unpublishes, changes schedules or rolls back; completed items stay published if a later one fails. On OutcomeUnknown, inspect the item before a new preview.

docs.title: Recovery and concurrency
docs.text:
Before mutation, the optional journal records the draft before-state, operation and fingerprint, then the outcome; a missing outcome means unknown completion. It cannot reverse publication. Referenced assets must stay in the asset store. Retention and backups are the host's job.

One operation gate covers inbound sync, export and planning, Pull/package/snapshot apply and durable jobs. With the backoffice package it also holds a cluster lease (cmsFerryLease row) so instances sharing a database run one operation at a time: claimed by conditional update and renewed every 30 seconds; waits until free (a canceled request gives up); lost two minutes after an instance stops; expiry uses UTC clocks, so keep them synchronized. Receiver-only hosts use a process-local gate.

Fingerprints reject changes before apply, but nothing locks other editors during an operation; coordinate on busy sites.

There is no implicit deletion, account replication, executable template/script deployment outside the opt-in optional modules, or guarantee that every third-party editor works without an adapter.

docs.title: Umbraco package integration decisions
docs.text: Based on Umbraco documentation reviewed on 2026-09-17; some older /extending and /reference links now redirect.

docs.title: Package layout and registration
docs.text:
Ferry uses Umbraco's recommended layout (NuGet distribution; library, tests and example website in one repository) with a .NET 10 / Umbraco 17.6.2 adapter project, under the Ferry Freeware License (free to use, closed source).

Referencing a package changes nothing by itself:

  • AddFerryUmbraco() registers the constrained text store (scoped, through IUmbracoBuilder.Services). No endpoints, no credential.
  • AddFerryUmbracoFull() selects the staged schema/language/content/media adapter.
  • The example website maps endpoints only when Ferry:Enabled is true.
  • Ferry:Backoffice:Enabled turns on the backoffice workspace, actions, queue and Management API. Destinations are configured on the server; credentials and payloads never reach the browser. The client uses Umbraco 17.6's authentication context.

Sources: Creating a Package, Example Package Repository, Dependency Injection, Composing.

docs.title: Draft persistence
docs.text:
The adapter saves with IContentService.Save and checks the result. It never publishes, unpublishes or schedules, and payloads carry no schedules. Target items that already have schedules are blocked, since a scheduled operation could publish the changed draft. Sort order and schema/media changes can still affect the live site.

API research used Umbraco 17.3.2 ContentService; the build targets 17.6.2. This is not a compatibility claim for all 17.x versions.

docs.title: Current capability boundary
docs.text:
• Constrained adapter: invariant text properties on existing matching document/data types.
  • Full adapter: staged schema and language transfer, variant draft content, mapper-based references and media.
  • Template code, arbitrary custom editors and unsupported tree operations must never be dropped silently.

Preview and apply run a whole-manifest preflight before writing, repeated at write boundaries. Backoffice export holds the operation gate for snapshot and asset staging, then releases it before remote requests. This is process-local, not a distributed transaction: external editors or another node can still race an operation. Database integration and locking must be established before a production release.

See the example website for a two-site sample.

docs.title: Receiver contract
docs.text:
The receiver accepts an optional legacy BearerToken, which grants every operation, or named peers with their own identity and operation scope. Either only authorizes receiver calls; neither grants Umbraco user, root or culture permissions.

Peer field Meaning Id Stable identity. Tokens One to eight rotation tokens. Enabled On/off. Revision Policy version; advance on every change. AllowedOperations Capabilities, Export, Preview, Apply, AssetRead, AssetWrite, PublicationPreview, PublicationApply, RecoveryRead. Empty grants nothing.

Tokens come from the host's secret provider (e.g. Ferry__Peers__0__Tokens__0), never source control:

builder.Configuration.AddEnvironmentVariables(); // or the host's managed secret provider
builder.Services.AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration(
    builder.Configuration.GetRequiredSection("Ferry"));

{
  "Ferry": {
    "Peers": [
      {
        "Id": "deployment-agent",
        "Enabled": true,
        "Revision": "2026-09-17",
        "AllowedOperations": [ "Capabilities", "Export", "Preview", "Apply" ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
  • Strict binding: unknown fields, bad or comma-combined operation names, numeric enums and malformed shapes fail startup.
  • Live reload: peers and the legacy token are re-read per request after a host reload; an invalid value fails closed. Parse failures and missed reloads are host concerns. Request and asset limits are startup-only.
  • Responses: Cache-Control: no-store on every request reaching authentication; bad or revoked token 401 (WWW-Authenticate: Bearer); missing operation 403.
  • Reauthorization happens inside the operation gate before any read or write, so queued requests see revocation.

docs.title: Capabilities and approvals
docs.text:
• Named peers see the adapter declaration narrowed to their operations, with asset read and write separate, plus a policy fingerprint and approval-token limit.
  • Their previews return an opaque envelope binding the fingerprint to peer id, policy hash, purpose (transfer or publication) and a 15-minute expiry, signed with a process-generated HMAC-SHA256 key.
  • Apply checks all of these before any journal, store or write. Bad or stale envelopes return 410 Gone; policy denials 403. Legacy peers keep raw fingerprints.
Decision Consequence Process-local key Restart invalidates approvals; multi-node needs preview/apply affinity. No replay ledger Envelopes are not single-use; the backoffice prepared-transfer store stays single-use. Revision in the hash Token rotation keeps envelopes valid; reusing an old revision can revive one, so always advance it. Fail closed over compatibility Strict older clients may reject the new fields; upgrade both peers.
